A Malibu mansion reportedly owned by actor Nicolas Cage looks a lot different after a huge sinkhole caused the driveway to collapse on Tuesday.

The sinkhole put dozens of homes at risk and made the area inaccessible for residents and emergency crews, according to Los Angeles news station KTLA.

Hurricane Marie, which didn’t reach land but still brought rain and high, dangerous surf to Southern California during the Labor Day holiday, is thought to have contributed to the sinkhole.

An unidentified homeowner in the gated community where the mansion is located told LAMag.com that people first noticed an eight-foot sinkhole at the mansion on Monday, but “thought it could be fixed pretty quickly.”

But then, the homeowner said, “all hell broke loose.”

LAMag said the sinkhole grew to 30 by 30 feet and “exposed a specific vulnerability” of waterfront homes in the area.

“The homes themselves are on pillars,” the homeowner explained. “The problem is that the driveway and the front part of the house are on soil. That’s what is vulnerable.”

Cage did not immediately reply to HuffPost’s request for comment.

Malibu officials issued an emergency proclamation saying the sinkhole has severely constrained emergency access and made the roadway “impassable.”

“The intact portion of the roadway is too narrow to accommodate emergency response vehicles, including fire engines and other large apparatus, creating a substantial risk to public safety and emergency response capabilities,” the proclamation said.

Realtor.com reports that Cage purchased the modern 4,000-square-foot beachfront mansion in 2024 at a cost of $10.5 million.
